builder_plan.scenario: Start with one repeated product task that has a measurable failure or cost.
builder_plan.change: Read the methods and identify one change you can isolate in that workflow.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current implementation on the same held-out tasks.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Successful outcomes, response time, human rework, and total cost per successful task.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: Large Language Models for Accurate Medical Chart Abstraction: Enabling Scalable and Secure Artificial Intelligence Deployment in Stroke
summary: The method replaces manual chart abstraction by non-expert staff for extracting structured clinical variables from unstructured neurointerventional reports. It requires infrastructure capable of running a 70B-parameter model (beyond a single 24 GB GPU without aggressive quantization or a third-party API) plus prompt engineering and expert adjudication of ambiguous cases. It can fail on inference-heavy variables such as intracranial angioplasty, and accuracy is conditioned on cases where the reference model produced a valid prediction, which may overstate real-world performance.
rationale: The accuracy is production-relevant for clinical data extraction, but the 24 GB GPU constraint and the need for expert oversight and workload-specific validation make a pilot deployment more appropriate than immediate adoption.

claims.statement: The method replaces manual chart abstraction by non-expert staff for extracting structured clinical variables from unstructured neurointerventional reports. It requires infrastructure capable of running a 70B-parameter model (beyond a single 24 GB GPU without aggressive quantization or a third-party API) plus prompt engineering and expert adjudication of ambiguous cases. It can fail on inference-heavy variables such as intracranial angioplasty, and accuracy is conditioned on cases where the reference model produced a valid prediction, which may overstate real-world performance.

LLaMA3.3-70B achieved 94.8% overall accuracy extracting eight clinical variables from stroke reports, with AI predictions more closely aligned with expert adjudication than non-expert annotations for most variables.
